_comment: Enzyme activity registry. enzymes: genotype_activity is the clearance multiplier for that phenotype relative to a normal metaboliser, back-derived where possible from the AUC ratio of a sensitive substrate that is named in the note; phenotype_frequency is European. perpetrators: residual enzyme activity is NOT stored - it is derived at load time from index_auc_ratio and the index substrate's own index_fm, as residual = (1/ratio - (1 - fm)) / fm, and checked against the FDA class band. Reading a residual straight off the AUC ratio would overstate the remaining activity. CAVEAT: ratios measured on ORALLY dosed index substrates include gut-wall inhibition and loss of first-pass extraction, so residuals derived from them overstate the purely hepatic effect; this applies to every CYP3A4 entry here. All values are from search excerpts of the cited sources and are unverified.

CYP2D6.note: Poor-metaboliser activity back-derived from atomoxetine, whose AUC is about 10-fold higher in poor metabolisers (a PBPK re-analysis gives 7.8-fold). Risperidone is deliberately NOT the anchor: its active moiety is CYP2D6-independent. Ultrarapid from the nortriptyline gene-copy series. Intermediate rests on the CPIC activity score of 0.5, not a measured AUC ratio. Frequencies are European and vary with a north-south gradient; reported poor-metaboliser rates span 1.5-7 %.

CYP2C19.note: Poor-metaboliser activity back-derived from omeprazole (AUC 7.5-fold in one study, 12-fold in another); ultrarapid (*17/*17) from a 2.1-fold LOWER omeprazole AUC. Intermediate and rapid rest on CPIC activity scores. European frequencies.

CYP2C9.note: Poor-metaboliser activity derived from a roughly 7-fold higher celecoxib steady-state exposure in *3/*3 (secondary source, unconfirmed). CPIC reclassified *2/*2 from poor to intermediate in 2020. Nordic European frequencies.

CYP3A4.note: No poor/intermediate/ultrarapid system exists for CYP3A4, so there is no genotype selector - only inhibition and induction. CYP3A5 expresser status is a separate axis not modelled here.

CYP1A2.note: No validated genotype-based activity multiplier; the *1F effect appears only alongside an inducer such as smoking, so no genotype selector is offered.

perpetrators.note: Index substrate: Reported in-vivo value whose primary URL could not be resolved; a fluconazole study implies at least 0.88. The value is phenotype-dependent.

perpetrators.name: Ciprofloxacin
perpetrators.note: Index substrate: Lower bound from the 33-fold AUC rise with fluvoxamine (range 14-103x).

perpetrators.name: Fluvoxamine
perpetrators.note: Range 14-103x. Index substrate: Lower bound from the 33-fold AUC rise with fluvoxamine (range 14-103x).

perpetrators.name: Ketoconazole 200 mg b.i.d.
perpetrators.note: Index substrate: Published static-model value. ORAL ratios also carry gut-wall CYP3A4 (ketoconazole raises oral midazolam 11-20x but intravenous only 2.7-4.7x), so a residual derived from an oral ratio OVERSTATES the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic.
